cards.claim: Mass is the amount of matter in a substance; weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object.
cards.quote: mass of a substance is the amount of matter present in it, while weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object.

cards.claim: Density is the amount of mass of a substance per unit volume.
cards.quote: Density of a substance is its amount of mass per unit volume.

cards.claim: The kelvin and celsius scales are related by K = °C + 273.15.
cards.quote: The kelvin scale is related to celsius scale as follows: K = °C + 273.15

cards.claim: Physical properties can be measured or observed without changing the identity or composition of a substance; measuring chemical properties requires a chemical change.
cards.quote: physical properties can be measured or observed without changing the identity or the composition of the substance. The measurement or observation of chemical properties requires a chemical change to occur.

cards.claim: Negative temperatures are possible on the Celsius scale but not on the Kelvin scale.
cards.quote: It is interesting to note that temperature below 0 °C (i.e., negative values) are possible in Celsius scale but in Kelvin scale, negative temperature is not possible.

cards.claim: Mass and weight are not interchangeable: the mass of a substance is constant, but its weight can vary from place to place as gravity changes.
cards.quote: The mass of a substance is constant, whereas, its weight may vary from one place to another due to change in gravity. You should be careful in using these terms.
